# Re-analysis using new cohort July 2026

```{r load.packages}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(vegan)
library(ecodist)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(glue)
library(tidyr)
```

# Prepare data

```{r read.in.new.data}
counts = read.csv("data/rh_abx_genus_level_counts.csv",
                  colClasses = c(public_client_id = "character"))

counts$days_in_program <- NULL

# Specifying colClass so leading 0 is not dropped
# Using this one bc I added stool vendor already
metadata = read.csv("data/abx_covariates_with_statins_a1c_all_covars.csv",
                    colClasses = c(public_client_id = "character"))

filtered_metadata = filter(metadata, public_client_id %in% counts$public_client_id)
```

```{r remove.zero.columns}
# Name is the variable for ASVs
# Value is their count
counts = counts %>% pivot_longer(-public_client_id) %>%  # Rows are person, ASVs count
  group_by(public_client_id) %>%                         # Groups by person
  group_by(name) %>%                                     # Group by taxa  
  mutate(total = sum(value)) %>%                         # Sums ASVS over all folks
  filter(total != 0) %>%                                 # Keep taxa that not 0
  ungroup() %>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = public_client_id) %>%
  as.data.frame()

# Add clients as row names, drop that id column
rownames(counts) <- counts$public_client_id
counts$public_client_id <- NULL

# Need to have it in matrix form for vegan
counts_matrix <- as.matrix(counts)
```

Now that we have a matrix, we should calculate our distance metric. Here I will 
use `avgdist` as this will subsample the data various times (rarefication). If 
your data is already rarefied, you can use `vegdist` instead. The `sample` 
argument should be set == to the minimum number of reads observed across your
samples. 

I also decided to save the dissimilarity matrix as an RDS file so that I can 
simply read it in for subsequent runs of this file. For example, if I want to 
run the entire notebook at once to produce my plot. Note you will need the `dist`
variable for the pcoa and the PERMANOVA. 

```{r calc.dist}
# Setting a seed for reproducibility
#set.seed(3) 
#dist <- avgdist(counts_matrix, dmethod = "bray", sample = 21869)

# Save an RDS file to skip distance calc in future
#saveRDS(dist, "rh_distance_matrix_beta_div.rds")
dist <- readRDS("data/rh_distance_matrix_beta_div.rds")
```

Noirceeeee. 

```{r calc.percent explained for plot}
# Calculate the variance explained by each coordinate
eigenvalues <- loaded_pcoa_result$eig
total_variance <- sum(eigenvalues[eigenvalues > 0])
percent_explained <- loaded_pcoa_result$eig / total_variance * 100
```

```{r}
# Create the scatter plot
# Here will just be looking at the first two coordinates
# Round to nearest digit after decimal, format nsmall = display 1 digit after "."
rounded_pe <- format(round(percent_explained[1:2], digits=1), nsmall=1)
coord_one_lab <- c(glue("Pco 1 ({rounded_pe[1]}%)"))
coord_two_lab <- c(glue("Pco 2 ({rounded_pe[2]}%)"))

my_palette <- c(
  "none" = "#007ea7", 
  "twelve" = "#80ced7", 
  "three" = "darkgrey"
)
```

```{r, fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
ordination_plot <- ggplot(
  pcoa_df,
  aes(x = pcoa1, y = pcoa2, color = abx_recency, fill = abx_recency)) +
  stat_ellipse(geom  = "polygon", alpha = 0.1, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha=0.8, shape= 21, stroke=0.6, color="black") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = my_palette) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = my_palette, guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title  = "PCoA",
    x      = coord_one_lab,
    y      = coord_two_lab,
    color = "Antibiotic use recency") +
  theme_minimal()
ordination_plot
ggsave(filename = "figures/rh_beta_diversity_pcoa_plot.pdf", plot = ordination_plot,
       width = 6, height = 4, units = "in")
```

# PERMANOVA

Now that we've made our plot and can see some group separation, we should test 
to see if this is statistically significant.

```{r add.stool.vendor}
merged_metadata <- merge(pcoa_df,
                         select(filtered_metadata, -abx_recency),
                         by = "public_client_id")

#saveRDS(merged_metadata, "data/merged_metadata_for_beta_div_PERMANOVA.rds")
```

Test!

```{r permanova}
merged_metadata$meds_blood_sugar <- factor(merged_metadata$meds_blood_sugar)
merged_metadata$meds_cholesterol <- factor(merged_metadata$meds_cholesterol)
merged_metadata$vendor_dashboard <- factor(merged_metadata$vendor_dashboard)

set.seed(3)
permanova_result <- adonis2(dist ~  age + sex + centered_BMI + 
                          meds_blood_sugar + meds_cholesterol + vendor_dashboard +
                          PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + centered_eGFR + abx_recency, 
                          data = merged_metadata, 
                          permutations = 9999)
print(permanova_result)
#saveRDS(permanova_result, "data/beta_div_PERMANOVA_result.rds")
```
Now do the pairwise comparisons since this was significant!

```{r pairwise.comparisons}
# Turn this from being a large dist object to a matrix
dist_matrix <- as.matrix(dist)

# Make sure rownames also match in metadata
rownames(merged_metadata) <- merged_metadata$public_client_id

# This creates an empty table to store the data
pairwise_results <- data.frame(  
  group1 = character(),
  group2 = character(),
  R2 = numeric(),
  pseudo_F = numeric(),
  p_value = numeric(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Loop over all pairwise combinations
groups <- unique(merged_metadata$abx_recency) # abx_recency == treatment

for (i in 1:(length(groups) - 1)) {
  for (j in (i + 1):length(groups)) {
    g1 <- groups[i]
    g2 <- groups[j]
    
    # This will subset to the groups you are comparing
    subset_meta <- merged_metadata[merged_metadata$abx_recency %in% c(g1, g2), ]
    subset_dist <- as.dist(dist_matrix[rownames(subset_meta), rownames(subset_meta)])
    
    result <- adonis2(subset_dist ~ age + sex + centered_BMI + 
                          meds_blood_sugar + meds_cholesterol + vendor_dashboard +
                          PC1 + PC2 + PC3 + PC4 + PC5 + centered_eGFR + abx_recency,
                      data = subset_meta, 
                      permutations =9999)
    p <- result$`Pr(>F)`[1]  
    R2 <- result$`R2`[1]
    pseudo_F <- result$`F`[1]

    pairwise_results <- rbind(pairwise_results, data.frame(
      group1 = g1,
      group2 = g2,
      p_value = p, 
      R2 = R2, 
      pseudo_F = pseudo_F))
  }
}

# FDR correction
pairwise_results$padj <- p.adjust(pairwise_results$p_value, method = "BH")

#saveRDS(pairwise_results, "data/beta_div_PERMANOVA_result_pairwise.rds")
```
